title: Vertical Adoption Pathways & Procurement Trigger Signals for Model Sourcing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a practical playbook that maps vertical-specific adoption pathways for inference (SMB SaaS, fintech, healthcare, regulated enterprise) and defines a set of procurement trigger signals that Sales/PD/customer success can use to escalate customers to Dedicated/Private offerings or to prioritize model onboarding. This is a tactical PM deliverable to reduce time-to-procurement, minimize missed contract revenue, and inform prioritized model compatibility work for the engineering backlog.
background: We have many one-off enterprise requests and mid-market deals that require rapid answers about model fit and procurement timing. Sales currently lacks a concise rubric to decide when to push for Dedicated contracts, when to recommend hosted with guardrails, and when to start Private onboarding. This ticket synthesizes competitive signals, usage telemetries, regional regulatory constraints, and procurement heuristics into a repeatable rubric and a heatmap product that can be instrumented in the Console.
outcomes: A 2-page playbook (playbook + quick checklist) for GTM and AE teams
A scored heatmap of verticals x procurement triggers (priority buckets)
A set of telemetry queries and alert thresholds for early warning in the Console
3 recommended product/engineering tickets to close top model compatibility gaps
acceptance_criteria: Playbook PDF uploaded to Confluence with executive summary and decision flow

2026-02-28: Conducted 6 customer interviews (AE-provided). Early signal: customers escalate when committed QPS > 30 and token spend > $20k/mo.
2026-03-04: Data team supplied anonymized telemetry sample (last 12 months). Building candidate procurement thresholds and model supply risk index.
2026-03-08: Draft heatmap prototype complete. Shared with PM leadership; requested clearer regional procurement triggers for EU-regulated healthcare customers.
2026-03-10: Incorporated legal input on data residency flags. Next: finalize playbook and create Eng tickets for kernel/quantization gaps identified.
competitive_signals_to_track: Availability of commercially licensable instruction-tuned variants (enterprise-friendly licenses)
Publicized quantization performance (4-bit/8-bit benchmarks) for throughput-sensitive workloads
Regional cloud marketplace listings and reseller partnerships (APAC/EU)
Announcements of evergreen enterprise SLAs or dedicated-host offers from competitors
Price tier changes for token pricing and embedding costs
procurement_trigger_rules: High QPS: sustained QPS > 30 for 7 days => evaluate Dedicated capacity
Cost trigger: forecasted monthly inference spend > $15k => Sales to propose reserved capacity options
Latency SLA: p95 latency requirement < 200ms and complexity of prompt (avg tokens > 200) => prioritize low-latency runtime variants
Data residency: presence of regulatory flag (EU healthcare/finance) => escalate to Private/VPC feasibility
Model availability risk: model supply risk index > 0.6 (license instability or frequent deprecation signals) => recommend multi-model fallback plan
methodology: Combine qualitative interviews (AE/SE/customer calls), telemetry analysis from Console usage logs, and competitive research. Score verticals on 6 axes (volume, latency sensitivity, data residency risk, procurement velocity, price sensitivity, model compatibility). Use weighted scoring to produce priority buckets (1-5).

risks: Telemetry gaps: some customers' token tagging is inconsistent which may undercount spend
Competitive noise: fast model releases could change supply risk quickly
Legal/regulatory ambiguity around what 'data residency' requires per customer
